formation.title: The Unification of Bavaria
formation.text:
The fractured lands of the Bavarian duchies are at last united under one banner. Munich, enriched by the salt trade and blessed by the Church, stands ready to lead a realm that stretches from the Alpine passes to the Danube plains. The question now is what kind of Bavaria we shall build. Shall we forge ourselves into the sword of the Catholic faith, marshalling our armies as the shield of orthodoxy against heresy? Or shall we follow the path of our Wittelsbach ancestors, masters of dynastic intrigue, patrons of art and learning, weaving alliances through marriage and culture rather than conquest?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the Shield of the Faith!

modifiers.name: The Catholic Shield
modifiers.text: Bavaria stands as the foremost defender of the Catholic faith in the Empire, its armies tempered by religious conviction and its people united in zealous orthodoxy.

options.text: The Wittelsbachs shall endure through statecraft.

modifiers.name: The Wittelsbach Inheritance
modifiers.text: The Wittelsbach dynasty has mastered the art of dynastic politics, weaving a web of marriages, alliances, and cultural patronage that extends Bavaria's influence far beyond its borders.

advances.name: Salt Road Tradition
advances.text: The ancient salt roads from Reichenhall and Berchtesgaden through Munich to Augsburg have made Bavaria wealthy. Controlling these routes is the foundation of Bavarian commerce.

advances.name: Alpine Pass Fortification
advances.text: Bavaria's southern border follows the Alpine passes, natural chokepoints that have been fortified since time immemorial to control trade and repel invaders.

advances.name: Hofbrau Tradition
advances.text: The court brewery tradition, culminating in the founding of the Hofbrauhaus, reflects both Bavarian economic ingenuity and the social importance of communal gathering places.

advances.name: Wittelsbach Court Culture
advances.text: The Wittelsbach dynasty cultivates a court of refined taste and cosmopolitan ambition, attracting artists and scholars from across Europe.

advances.name: Landshut Reunification
advances.text: The Landshut War of Succession ended the centuries of Bavarian partition. Under Albrecht IV's primogeniture law of 1506, the duchy became forever indivisible.

event.title: The Reunification of Bavaria
event.text: The Landshut War of Succession has ended. After years of conflict between the rival Wittelsbach lines of Bavaria-Munich and Bavaria-Landshut, the dynasty's lands are reunited for the first time in generations. Duke Albrecht IV has triumphed, but the cost has been heavy, Imperial arbitration has stripped away some territories, and the estates demand concessions. The duke now proposes a revolutionary measure: a primogeniture law that would make the duchy forever indivisible. The estates, gathered in assembly, weigh their response. Shall the duchy embrace strict primogeniture, concentrating all power in a single line? Or shall the estates exact a compact, trading their consent for guaranteed rights of representation?

options.text: One duke, one Bavaria: indivisible and eternal.

modifiers.name: Primogeniture Law
modifiers.text: The law of indivisibility ensures the Bavarian lands pass intact to a single heir, ending centuries of ruinous partition.

options.text: The Landtag shall have its voice.

modifiers.name: Landtag Compact
modifiers.text: The estates of Bavaria have agreed to a compact with the duke, trading obedience for representation and creating a stable system of governance.

advances.name: Munich Staple Rights
advances.text: Munich's staple right requires all salt passing through the city to be offered for sale before continuing its journey, enriching the capital and cementing its role as Bavaria's commercial heart.

advances.name: Rentmeister System
advances.text: The division of Bavaria into administrative districts headed by Rentmeisters created an efficient system of tax collection and regional governance.

advances.name: Catholic League
advances.text: Founded by Maximilian I in 1609, the Catholic League united Catholic Imperial princes under Bavarian leadership, fielding one of the most formidable armies of the Thirty Years' War.

event.title: The Catholic League
event.text: As Protestant princes form their Union and heresy spreads across the Empire, Duke Maximilian I of Bavaria has answered with the founding of the Catholic League. This alliance of Catholic Imperial princes, bankrolled by Bavarian wealth and led by Bavarian resolve, stands as the mightiest military force in Catholic Germany. Under the brilliant command of Count Tilly, the League's army of 25,000 men (well-drilled, well-supplied, and burning with confessional zeal) has already proven itself on the battlefield. The question is how Bavaria shall wield this formidable instrument: as a hammer of military force to crush Protestant resistance, or as a diplomatic tool backed by Jesuit persuasion to reclaim souls through education and conversion?

options.text: Let Tilly's armies speak for the faith.

modifiers.name: Catholic League Arms
modifiers.text: The military apparatus of the Catholic League provides Bavaria with disciplined infantry and ample manpower to defend the faith.

options.text: The Jesuits shall be our finest weapon.

modifiers.name: Jesuit Diplomacy
modifiers.text: The Society of Jesus serves as Bavaria's diplomatic instrument, its colleges educating loyal administrators and its missions extending Bavarian influence across Catholic Europe.

advances.name: Jesuit Colleges
advances.text: The Society of Jesus established colleges throughout Bavaria that served as instruments of both education and Counter-Reformation, training loyal administrators and reconverting Protestant populations.

advances.name: Maximilian's Fiscal Reforms
advances.text: Duke Maximilian I reorganized Bavarian finances with unprecedented rigor, creating a war chest that funded the Catholic League and made Bavaria the strongest Catholic principality.

advances.name: Bavarian Standing Army
advances.text: Established by Elector Maximilian II Emanuel in 1682, the permanent Bavarian Army replaced temporary levies with professional soldiers, including the distinctive Chevaulegers cavalry.

advances.name: Baroque Patronage
advances.text: The Wittelsbach electors transformed Munich into a Baroque masterpiece, commissioning the Theatine Church, Nymphenburg Palace, and the expansion of the Residenz.

event.title: Baroque Munich
event.text: A transformation is sweeping through Munich. The Theatine Church rises over the skyline, its Italian Baroque facade a testament to the dynasty's ambitions. At Nymphenburg, a summer palace of astonishing grandeur takes shape amid formal gardens that rival Versailles. The Wittelsbach court has become a beacon of artistic patronage, Italian architects, Flemish painters, and German musicians flock to Bavaria's capital. The Residenz grows ever more magnificent with each generation of builders. What was once a modest ducal seat among many in the Empire has become one of Europe's foremost cultural capitals, its buildings proclaiming Bavarian power and Catholic splendor to all who behold them.

options.text: Munich shall rival the great courts of Europe.

advances.name: Salt Monopoly
advances.text: The ducal monopoly on Bavarian salt production concentrated enormous wealth in state hands, funding military adventures and cultural patronage alike.

advances.name: Montgelas Reforms
advances.text: Count Montgelas modernized Bavaria from 1799, abolishing feudal privileges, secularizing church lands, introducing civil equality, and creating a modern bureaucratic state.

advances.name: Kingdom Sovereignty
advances.text: Elevated to a kingdom by Napoleon in 1806, Bavaria achieved full sovereignty for the first time, reorganizing its military along modern lines and establishing itself as a European power in its own right.

advances.name: Reinheitsgebot Industry
advances.text: The industrialization of Bavarian brewing combines centuries of purity-law expertise with modern techniques, coal-fired malt kilns, mechanical processes, and rail distribution to produce beer at unprecedented scale.

destiny.name: Bavarian Destiny
destiny.text: United Bavaria stands at a crossroads. The destiny of the Wittelsbach realm, whether forged in the fires of Catholic zeal or shaped by dynastic cunning, now lies in our hands.

event.title: The Bavarian Destiny
event.text: Bavaria is formed, and our chosen path lies ahead. The traditions of our ancestors guide us, but it is we who must forge the future. Whether through the sword or through statecraft, the Wittelsbach name shall echo through the ages.

destiny.name: The Salzburg Crusade
destiny.text: Secure the great Catholic bishopric of Salzburg and the Imperial city of Augsburg to anchor Bavaria's position as the foremost defender of the faith in southern Germany.

event.title: The Salt and the Sword
event.text: Salzburg, the ancient prince-bishopric whose salt mines once rivalled our own, now flies the Bavarian banner. And Augsburg (that great Imperial city where the fateful Confession was read, where Catholic and Protestant first drew their theological battle lines) has been brought into our fold. With the wealth of Salzburg's mines and the commercial might of Augsburg's bankers secured, Bavaria's position as the Catholic champion of the south is beyond question. The salt roads and the sword roads are now one.

destiny.name: The Palatinate Claim
destiny.text: Seize Heidelberg and the Palatinate electorate, as Maximilian I did after the Battle of White Mountain, establishing Bavaria as the premier military power among the Catholic princes.

event.title: The Palatinate Electorate
event.text: Heidelberg has fallen. The seat of the Palatinate, once the stronghold of Calvinist heresy and the spark that ignited the great religious wars, is now ours. As Maximilian I seized the electoral dignity from Frederick V after the Battle of White Mountain, so too have we claimed what was rightfully owed to Catholic valor. The question is how we shall consolidate this triumph. Shall we emulate Tilly's hammer, forging our armies into an unstoppable instrument of conquest? Or shall we raise the League's banner high, inspiring Catholic princes across the Empire to rally to our cause?

modifiers.name: Tilly's Hammer
modifiers.text: The army has been forged into an instrument of devastating efficiency, trained in the methods of the great Count Tilly, rapid recruitment and relentless morale, though the cost of such a war machine strains the treasury.

options.text: Rally the princes to our banner.

modifiers.name: League Banner
modifiers.text: Under the banner of the Catholic League, Bavaria's armies reinforce swiftly and fight with the fury of men who believe God is on their side.

destiny.name: Catholic Supremacy
destiny.text: Bring both Prague and Vienna under Bavarian dominion, eclipsing the Habsburgs themselves as the supreme Catholic power in Central Europe.

event.title: Catholic Imperium
event.text: Prague and Vienna both bow to the Bavarian lion. The Defenestration of Prague once plunged Europe into decades of war, now that city's spires gleam under Wittelsbach authority. And Vienna, seat of the Habsburgs for centuries, has yielded to a greater Catholic power. Bavaria has achieved what even the most ambitious of its dukes never dared dream: supremacy over the entire Catholic heartland of Central Europe. Shall we build an imperium of fortresses and supply lines to hold these vast conquests, or pursue a strategy of swift wars and decisive victories to keep our enemies perpetually off balance?

modifiers.name: Catholic Imperium
modifiers.text: A vast network of fortresses secures Bavaria's Catholic empire, with supply lines stretching across Central Europe; though diplomatic finesse has been sacrificed for military dominion.

options.text: Strike swiftly, like at White Mountain.

modifiers.name: White Mountain Doctrine
modifiers.text: The doctrine of swift, decisive warfare, as practiced at the Battle of White Mountain, allows Bavaria to press claims rapidly and negotiate from strength, though domestic construction suffers from the military focus.

destiny.name: The Golden Treasury
destiny.text: Establish Bavaria's financial foundations on salt, as the dukes did when they made the Reichenhall trade their monopoly: a Salzkontor in three towns, and a formidable treasury worthy of Wittelsbach ambition.

event.title: The Wittelsbach Treasury
event.text: The vaults of Munich overflow. Through the salt houses of the ducal monopoly and careful stewardship of our realm's resources, Bavaria has accumulated wealth that would make the Fuggers themselves take notice. The salt revenues of Reichenhall, the brewing profits, the careful management of ducal estates: all have contributed to a treasury that gives the Wittelsbachs options that raw military power alone could never provide. Gold opens doors that swords cannot.

options.text: Wealth is the foundation of all power.

destiny.name: Cultural Metropolis
destiny.text: Transform the capital into a cultural center: a city in rank and not only in name, with an Arts Academy for the court's painters and sculptors, and an international reputation cultivated.

event.title: Munich Ascendant
event.text: Munich has outgrown its old walls and is counted among the cities of the Empire. Its Arts Academy trains painters and sculptors whose work is sought across Europe. The Wittelsbach court has become a magnet for artists, philosophers, and men of learning. Munich is no longer merely the capital of a German duchy. It is becoming a European cultural center in its own right. Shall we focus on building Munich into a true academy city, drawing the finest minds to our court? Or shall we extend the Wittelsbach diplomatic network, weaving alliances and dynastic ties across the continent?

options.text: Munich shall be an academy for all Europe.

modifiers.name: Munich Academy
modifiers.text: Munich's academies and salons draw scholars and artists from across Europe, spreading Bavarian cultural influence and assimilating new populations into the Wittelsbach fold.

options.text: Extend the Wittelsbach web of alliances.

modifiers.name: Wittelsbach Network
modifiers.text: The Wittelsbach diplomatic network spans the continent, binding allies and subjects to Bavaria through marriage, treaty, and mutual obligation; though maintaining such a web leaves less coin for hired swords.

destiny.name: Wittelsbach Zenith
destiny.text: Achieve the pinnacle of Wittelsbach power: a vast treasury, unmatched prestige, and Munich rebuilt as Ludwig I rebuilt it, with new quarters, the Ludwigstrasse and the Konigsplatz. Requires Munich held and raised to 54 development.

conditions.text: We own Munich and its development is at least 54

event.title: The Wittelsbach Zenith
event.text: The Wittelsbach dynasty has reached its apex. A treasury overflowing with gold, a realm of unmatched prestige, a capital twice the town it was: Bavaria has transcended its origins as a frontier duchy to become one of Europe's great powers through culture, diplomacy, and economic might rather than conquest alone. King Ludwig's vision of Munich as the 'Athens on the Isar' is no longer a dream but a reality. The Glyptothek and Pinakothek stand as monuments to a civilization that chose to build rather than destroy. Shall we crown this achievement with a golden age of arts and urban splendor, or pursue a grand dynastic vision that reshapes the political map of Europe?

options.text: Let Munich become the Athens on the Isar.

modifiers.name: Athens on the Isar
modifiers.text: Munich has become the Athens on the Isar, a city of magnificent architecture, efficient administration, and cultural splendor, though the scholarly court has little patience for military logistics.

options.text: The Wittelsbach vision shall reshape Europe.

modifiers.name: Ludwig's Vision
modifiers.text: King Ludwig's grand vision of a prosperous, stable, self-sufficient Bavaria has been realized, a realm where separatism is unknown and the people are well-fed, though the nation's pacifist reputation makes war a costly endeavor.

units.name: Bavarian Ritter
units.text: Heavy armored cavalry drawn from the Bavarian lesser nobility, the Ritter charge with devastating force in the feudal tradition of the Imperial knights.

units.name: Kreisinfanterie
units.text: Disciplined infantry of the Imperial Circle, drilled in the Spanish tercio tradition and hardened by the religious wars. They fight with the conviction of men defending their faith.

units.name: Bavarian Chevaulegers
units.text: Light cavalry of the Bavarian standing army, in the French-influenced tradition of the Bavarian military. Trained for reconnaissance and pursuit, and in the wars of Napoleon the whole of the Bavarian line cavalry, so it is drilled to charge home as well.

buildings.name: Salzkontor
buildings.text: A salt trading house that manages the purchase, storage, and distribution of Bavaria's most valuable commodity along the ancient salt roads.

buildings.name: Jesuitenkolleg
buildings.text: A college of the Society of Jesus, combining rigorous classical education with Counter-Reformation theology to train loyal Catholic administrators and scholars.

buildings.name: Hofbrauhaus
buildings.text: The court brewery serves as both an economic enterprise and a social institution, producing fine Bavarian beer while providing a gathering place that promotes civic loyalty.

buildings.name: Barockschloss
buildings.text: A magnificent Baroque palace in the Wittelsbach tradition, proclaiming the dynasty's cultural ambitions through Italian architecture, formal gardens, and lavish interior decoration.

buildings.name: Salzstadel
buildings.text: The staple house where every load of salt passing through the city is stored, weighed and offered for sale before it may travel on.

children.text: Salt is produced in the market

buildings.name: Brauerei
buildings.text: An industrial-scale brewery producing beer under the Reinheitsgebot purity law, consuming vast quantities of wheat, barley and coal.

buildings.name: Mariensaule
buildings.text: A towering Marian column erected in the heart of the city, proclaiming Bavaria's devotion to the Virgin Mary and its triumph over heresy, plague, and foreign invasion.

buildings.name: Glyptothek
buildings.text: A neoclassical museum housing a magnificent collection of Greek and Roman sculpture, embodying King Ludwig I's vision of Munich as the cultural capital of Europe.

list.name: Geheimer Rat
list.text: Established by Albert IV in 1488 and reorganised by Albert V in 1570, the Geheimer Rat became the central executive council of the Bavarian duchy. A small body of trained jurists prepared decrees for the duke, supervised the chancellery, and from 1620 ran the wartime government of Maximilian I, displacing the older Hofrat as the seat of executive power in Munich.

list.name: Hofkammer
list.text: The Aulic Chamber of Munich, reorganised by Wilhelm IV in the 1530s and again by Maximilian I after 1598, ran the Wittelsbach regalia: the Reichenhall and Traunstein salt monopoly, the customs at Wasserburg and Burghausen, the ducal Munzamt, and the proceeds of crown estates. Its disciplined accounts made the Bavarian salt revenues one of the richest regalian incomes in the Empire and bankrolled the Catholic League.

list.name: Bavarian Landstaende
list.text: The Bavarian Estates Diet of prelates, nobles, and town deputies that met irregularly at Munich and Landshut from the fourteenth century. The Landtag of 1577 produced the Landesfreiheitserklarung, the territorial charter formalising estate rights to consent to extraordinary taxation. The Diet co-governed the duchy with its dukes until Maximilian I's wartime emergencies sidelined it after 1620, and it was finally dissolved by Montgelas's reforms in 1808.

list.name: Geistlicher Rat
list.text: The Ecclesiastical Council established by Albert V in 1570 to direct the duchy's hard turn toward the Counter-Reformation. Staffed by Jesuit-trained councillors, it supervised episcopal nominations, licensed printers, ran the Bavarian seminaries, and oversaw the network of Jesuit colleges at Ingolstadt, Munich, Dillingen, and Landshut. Under Maximilian I, Bavaria became the Catholic League's intellectual arsenal.

list.name: Hofmarken
list.text: The Bavarian system of patrimonial seigneurial jurisdiction codified in the Landrecht of 1518 and successive Landgerichtsordnungen, by which abbeys, knights, and noble landholders exercised lower courts, police powers, and tax collection over their tenants. The rentmeister coordinated, but the Hofmarksherren ran daily justice, and the system survived every reform until its abolition by the Bavarian constitution of 1818.
